title: Trigonometry: Choosing Law of Sines or Law of Cosines Practice
description: Practice identifying triangle cases, choosing the first law, and explaining the reason before solving.

questions.question: A triangle has A = 42 degrees, B = 63 degrees, and side a = 14. Which case is this?
questions.explanation: Two angles and a non-included side are known, so the case is AAS.

questions.question: For the AAS data A = 42 degrees, B = 63 degrees, and a = 14, which law should be used first?
options: Either law before finding another part
questions.explanation: AAS gives enough angle information and a complete pair A with a, so the Law of Sines is the direct first law.

questions.question: A triangle has sides a = 9, b = 12, and included angle C = 58 degrees. Which law should start the solution?
options: Law of Sines, because two sides are known
Law of Cosines, because this is SAS
Law of Sines, because C is known
questions.explanation: The known angle C is included between sides a and b, so this is SAS. SAS starts with the Law of Cosines to find side c.

questions.question: A triangle has side lengths 6, 8, and 11. Which first move is best?
options: Use Law of Cosines to find an angle
Find the third angle by subtracting from 180 degrees
Use tangent with the longest side
questions.explanation: Three sides are known, so the case is SSS. SSS starts with the Law of Cosines to find an angle.

questions.question: If a problem gives ASA information, the Law of Sines is usually ready after finding the third angle if needed.
questions.explanation: ASA gives two angles and one side. The third angle completes an opposite angle-side pair, so the Law of Sines is the natural first method.

questions.question: A triangle has A = 35 degrees, a = 10, and b = 16. What annotation should come before solving?
options: SSA; Law of Sines first, with an ambiguous-case check
AAS; find the third angle first
questions.explanation: The given angle A is opposite known side a, and another side b is known. This is SSA, so use Law of Sines only after checking the ambiguous case.

questions.question: Fill in the first law only: For SAS data, use the Law of ____ first.
questions.explanation: SAS has two sides and the included angle but no complete opposite pair, so it starts with the Law of Cosines.

questions.question: After a SAS problem uses the Law of Cosines to find the third side, why might either law become possible?
options: The problem now has more known parts, possibly including complete opposite pairs
All remaining angles must be equal
questions.explanation: After the first missing side is found, the triangle has more known information. If a complete opposite pair is available, Law of Sines can be used; Law of Cosines can also continue from side lengths.

questions.question: Annotate this problem before solving: In triangle ABC, A = 46 degrees, C = 59 degrees, and b = 20. State the case, first law, and reason.
questions.correctAnswer: This is ASA because two angles and the included side are known. Use the Law of Sines first after finding B, because then side b has its opposite angle B as a complete pair.
questions.explanation: A strong annotation names ASA, chooses Law of Sines, and explains that finding the third angle creates the complete pair B and b.
